context.alert_text: Memory utilisation of the orders API service above 90 percent

root_cause.hypothesis: The 07:38:02 deploy (task definition revision 19, replacing 18) changed the ECS task memory/Node.js heap settings such that the container's 512MiB memory limit is too close to the configured Node heap cap, causing the app to hit heap OOM under load. This drives memory utilization to the alarm threshold and causes the rolling deployment to fail tasks repeatedly (only 1/3 desired tasks running, 9 failed deployment tasks), while the container image itself is unchanged.
ruled_out: No unrelated cluster-wide change: C2 shows no other change on the cluster in the prior 6h, so this is isolated to the orders-api deploy.
Not a code/image regression: D1 shows image and previous_image are identical (2.14.1), only the task definition revision changed.

proposal.reasoning: The memory alarm and OOM heap errors correlate directly with the task definition change (revision 19) deployed just before the alert; the container image itself did not change, pointing to a task-def-level regression (e.g., memory/heap config) rather than application code. Rolling back to the prior task definition revision (18) that was stable removes the suspect change while a human investigates the NODE_OPTIONS/memory sizing.
proposal.expected_effect: Service returns to the previously stable task definition (revision 18), memory utilization should drop below threshold, failed task launches should stop, and desired task count (3) should be reached.

reasons: Passed all policies. Held for operator approval before execution.
